result:
PR #71 opened: https://github.com/FChecklist/claude-control/pull/71

**Final checkpoint:**

Of the 105 gap-analysis items, **12 were real corrections** (not_implemented → partially_implemented) — the original analysis had missed two live prior-art systems: a working "Prompt OS" in compliance-tracker (real `prompt_templates`/`prompt_versions`/`prompt_eval_*` tables used at ~20 production call sites, with admin-gated versioning, LLM-scored eval runs, and an audit trigger) and real pgvector+HNSW embedding-similarity/semantic-cache infrastructure. **93 items held up** under independent re-verification, including all 10 of the highest naming-collision-risk items (business rule, permission, policy, compliance, governance, audit, cost, dependency, gateway integration, knowledge sync) — confirmed via direct code reads, not softened. Final count: 73 not_implemented, 32 partially_implemented, 0 already_implemented (was 85/20/0).

Every one of the 10 surviving phases now has an explicit `integration_point` naming a real Wiring Engine table entity, the Capability Registry, or a named gateway (G01–G10) — except phase_10 (docs-only) and part of phase_8 (translation/localization/marketplace/import/export engines with zero prior art anywhere), both explicitly justified as standalone. No phase was removed, but phase_1 was substantially rescoped: it originally planned to build a *new* SQLite `prompt_registry` table, which would have been exactly the duplicate parallel system the Owner's directive was meant to prevent — it now extends the real, live Postgres tables instead. `scripts/generate_wiring_registry.py` still exits 0.
